subtopic: Building insurance and an emergency fund
subtype: Approach: buying a policy only for tax saving [Pitfall]
passage:
28 March. An agent phoned Gurpreet at closing time: "Sign today and you save tax, only this week." The plan cost 40,000 a year. Gurpreet signed on the phone, tired and relieved to have it done.
June. Hafsa, a colleague, asked what the plan covered. Gurpreet had never read the paper. Together they went through it. If something happened, the payout would be only 4,00,000. Gurpreet went quiet: ten years of premiums for that.
The next March. When the agent phoned again, Gurpreet said, "Send me the papers, I'll read them and call you." Hafsa sat beside Gurpreet with a highlighter, and the pages came out marked with questions, not signatures.

qa.q: How much did the plan cost each year?
What was Gurpreet feeling in June when reading the paper with Hafsa?
qa.a: Gurpreet was dismayed and felt foolish, shown by going quiet on seeing how little the payout was for ten years of premiums.

qa.q: What could Gurpreet try before buying anything late in the next March?
qa.a: Gurpreet could start comparing plans early in the year and ask a registered adviser what protection each one gives.

qa.q: How might Hafsa have seen Gurpreet's rushed purchase?
qa.a: Hafsa probably saw a tired colleague pushed by a deadline, not careless, and so offered to read the paper together.

grounding: The passage shows a person buying a low-cover plan under an agent's late-March push for tax benefits, then finding it gives little protection for the premium.
